segments.translation: Just right over in the other hollow—Cloud Hollow. Where the church is, up that hollow. Down that way, I was born. We moved around in that area when I was growing up. The last time we moved it was straight from where the church is at the end of the hollow is. Still there—that is where we lived. And when we moved from there “Let's move for good from here,” our dad said. “We are going to travel.” We came across. Grandfather lived across by the hollow little ridge. We came there. And then, “We are moving from this hollow”, he told him. “Why? You all have been living around here a long time.” he said. “That is true. It has to be. I am going to get closer to my work.” And then we came up through the hollow. Dropping things. We came over. Then we went back into another hollow. And, where we came out, there was a little house, close. It was just this wide [gestures]. “We can live there until the summer,” he said. And water and food—there is a creek. “You all can fish there or catch crawdads. And in the evening we will eat good.” We would go there. Norman would follow us all the time. Second— in the family we were half brothers, that one. My dad was his dad, that one. His mom lived nearby. But they moved when we got there. So he stayed with us. He would be with us when we would go to the water. We would go catch lots of fish. We would eat fast, in the evening. He had a sawmill, that boss. My dad worked there. And we would go to the water every day. And then, about two years we lived there, their sawmill broke down. “I guess that’s all for us,” they said. “I guess we will go back, then.” ‘Loaded up and came back up the hollow. We came back down, close to Grandfather’s house. We came back again. [Grandfather said] “That house is still there—where you all lived.” “We are headed back to it,” he said. So, we went back over there. Then they said “Let's make a church on the hill.” They said, “There, before Anigvluyo.” It was flat. And that was our church. We would walk that far. And went there on Sunday or Saturday. At night we would be coming back. And come back there [to the original house]. It was closer for us to go, when we moved there. Then they talked about making a church right there on the hill. “On the ridge,” they said. Then they started cutting wood up, the adults. And was dragging limbs around, clearing for the workers. We made it. My dad’s brother had a sawmill there. He started milling. He milled all that, where that little building is. We made a church there. We went in there. Jen was an old lady then, she would walk using her cane. She would come up. It was like this, there. She would come in on Sunday morning.

segments.text: ᎯᎾᏃ ᏙᎯᏳᎯ Ꮫ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎨᎵᎰ ᏥᏲᏎᎰ ᏦᏍᏛᏓᏅᏟ. ᎠᏯᏛ ᎠᎦᏛᎦᏅ ᏍᎪᎯᏍᏆ ᏂᎦᏚ ᎠᎾᏗᏍᎪ ᎠᏬᎮᎸ. ᎠᏭ ᎡᎯ ᎠᏫᏄᏥ ᎣᎩᎾᏝᏃᎮᏢ ᎯᎸᏍᎩ ᏄᎲ “ᎯᎪᎥᏍ ᎨᎮ Ꮎ ᎠᎩᏴᎵᎨ ᏣᏂᏃᎮᏍᎪ?” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “Who Jennie?” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Yeah,” ᏍᎨᎦ ᎠᏬᎮᎸ ᏃᏗᏍ ᏜᏱᎪ ᏩᏪᏙᎸ ᏔᎵ ᏄᏒ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎪᏪᎳ ᏙᎩᏂᎪᎵᏰᎥ ᎠᏫ ᎡᎯ ᎠᏫᏄᏣ ᎤᏛᎾ ᎾᏅ “Jennie Birdchopper,--” ᎪᏪᎸ ᏣᏗᎲ “--birthday hundred and forty-four years old.” -- “I believe it!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎾᎯᏳ. “ᎰᏩ Ꮫ ᎨᎵ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏧᏲᎱᏒᎾ ᏫᎨᏙᎲ ᏍᏊ ᎤᎾᏅ ᏍᎫ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎤᎾᎾ ᎣᏍᏓᏝᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᎤᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩ ᏚᏩᎧᎭ ᎠᏫᏴ ᏴᏱᎦᎾᏕᏂ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏂᏕᎬᏁᎲ ᏕᎦᏅᎬᎵᎲ ᎤᎾ ᎦᎧᎲ “ᎠᏎᏗ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏱᏂᏣᏛᎦ ᏃᏭ” ᎨᎪᏎᎸ “ᏃᎨᏒ Ꮓ ᎦᎵᏦᏕᏭ ᏛᎨᏏ ᏓᎦᏣᏪᏐᎸᏍᏛᏂ ᏃᏭ” ᎨᎪᎮᎸ. ᎾᎯᏳᏭᏅᏍ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏗ ᎨᎵᎲ “ᏓᎦᏣᏪᏐᎸᏍᏛᏂ ᏃᏭ” ᎨᎪᎮᎸ “ᎠᎭᏂᏭ ᎢᏥᏙᎾᎡᏍᏗ” ᏭᏴᏢ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎦᏥᎦᏙᏍᏙ ᏥᏙᎬ Ꮓ ᏦᏍᏓᏁᎶᏂᏙ ᎤᎷᏨ. “Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎯᎦᏙᏍᏗ?” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “Ꮎ ᎤᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩ ᏥᏚᏝᏃᎮᏛ ᏥᏂ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ. “Ꭳ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎤᎾ ᎦᎧᎰ ᏧᏙᏙᏮᏗ ... ᎠᏎᎾ ᎦᎵᏦᏕᏭ ᏛᎨᏏ ᏛᎦᏣᏪᏐᎸᏍᏛᏁᏏ ᏥᏕᎪᏏ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᏓᏍᏛᏰᎯ ᏛᎮ” ᎤᏛᏅ ᎠᏎᏛ “ᎠᏩ Ꭸ ᎠᎹᏯᏫᏁᏓ bucket ᏔᎵ ᏙᏗᎩ ᎤᏕᏂᏁᎦ” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “ᎰᏩ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ five gallon ᏓᏟᏍᏛ ᎯᏍᎩ ᏳᏟᎶᏗ ᏚᏩᎧᎲ ᏫᏙᎩᏂᎩᏒ ᏙᏗᏲᎩᏂᎾᏝᏛᏅ ᏙᎩᏂᏅ ᎤᎾᎾ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬᏂ ᎳᎵ ᏣᏃᏎᎰ ᏐᎢᎲ ᏅᏥ ᏥᏚᏙᎥ. ᎤᎾᏃᏅ “ᎢᏣᎵᏍᏓᏴᎲᎦ!” ᎤᏛᎾ ᏃᏭᏅ “ᏥᏂ Ꮫ ᏰᏥᏰᏍᏓᎾ ᏱᏓᎵᏍᏓᏴᎲᎦ ᏪᏥᎥᏏ ᎴᏱᎦ ᎤᎩᏍᏗ ᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏍ ᎮᎾ ᏙᏯ” ᎤᏂᏄᎸᏅ ᎤᏂᏰᏍᏙᏗ ᎠᏫ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏓᏂᏙᎲ ᎠᏍᎪᎵ ᎾᏅᏁᎲ ᏗᎧᏃᎨᏂ ᏃᎴ ᏯᏂᏌᎳᏓᏂ ᎾᏅᏁᎰ ᎠᎾᏒᏂᎵᏙᎰ “ᎠᏂᎨ ᏥᏂ” ᎤᎾᏛᎾ Ꮓ “ᎨᏍᏛ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏯᏛᏁ ᎠᏫ Ꮫ ᏗᏝ ᏥᎦᏂᏝ ᏳᏪᏥᏂᏏᏂ” ᎤᏅᏛᏅ Ꭰ ᏄᏅᏁᎵ ᏂᎬ Ꮫ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᎨᏍᏕ ᏧᎪᎵ ᏱᏚᎴ Ꮲ ᏂᎦᏓ Ꭰ ᏱᏂᎬᏁᎵ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏗᎵᏍᏈᏛᏍᎪ ᏃᎴ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏱᏣᏌᎵᏓᏂ ᏍᎫ ᏍᎩ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲ ᏫᏂᎾᎬᎸᎲᏭᏅ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏭᏂᎩᏒ ᎤᎾ ᏭᏂᏅᏃ ᏭᏂᏰᏍᏛᎾ ᎤᏠᏳᏭ ᏰᎦᏟ ᏴᏰᏍᏛᏍᎩ ᏍᎫ ᏄᏅᏁᎸ ᎤᏂᏰᏍᏛᎾ
segments.transliteration: hinano dohiyuhi dv agayvlige geliho tsiyoseho tsosdvdanvtli. ayadv agadvganv sgohisqua nigadu anadisgo awohelv. awu ehi awinutsi oginatlanohetlv hilvsgi nuhv “higovs gehe na agiyvlige tsaninohesgo?” awohelv “Who Jennie?” tsiyohelv “Yeah,” sgega awohelv nodis dlayigo wawedolv tali nusv tsigesv gowela doginigoliyev awi ehi awinutsa udvna nanv “Jennie Birdchopper,--” gowelv tsadihv “--birthday hundred and forty-four years old.” -- “I believe it!” tsiyohelv nahiyu. “howa dv geli” tsiyohelv tsuyohusvna wigedohv squu unanv sgu nahiyu unana osdatlanohesgv unitsilvsgi duwakaha awiyv yvyiganadeni osda nidegvnehv deganvgvlihv una gakahv “asedi eliwu yinitsadvga nowu” gegoselv “nogesv no galitsodewu dvgesi dagatsawesolvsdvni nowu” gegohelv. nahiyuwunvs yiga adi gelihv “dagatsawesolvsdvni nowu” gegohelv “ahaniwu itsidonaesdi” wuyvtlv galitsode gatsigadosdo tsidogv no tsosdanelonido ulutsv. “do usdi higadosdi?” awohelv “na unitsilvsgi tsidutlanohedv tsini” tsiyohelv. “o nigolv una gakaho tsudodowvdi ... asena galitsodewu dvgesi dvgatsawesolvsdvnesi tsidegosi” tsiyohelv “dasdvyehi dvhe” udvnv asedv “awa ge amayawineda bucket tali dodigi udeninega” awohelv “howa” tsiyohelv five gallon datlisdv hisgi yutlilodi duwakahv widoginigisv dodiyogininatladvnv dogininv unana adasdayvhvsgvni lali tsanoseho soihv nvtsi tsidudov. unanonv “itsalisdayvhvga!” udvna nowunv “tsini dv yetsiyesdana yidalisdayvhvga wetsivsi leyiga ugisdi dulvwisdas hena doya” uninulvnv uniyesdodi awi nigalisdanidohv asgoli nanvnehv dikanogeni nole yanisaladani nanvneho anasvnilidoho “anige tsini” unadvna no “gesdv gusdi yadvne awi dv ditla tsiganitla yuwetsinisini” unvdvnv a nunvneli nigv dv nulisdvnv gesde tsugoli yidule tlv nigada a yinigvneli nigada dilisquidvsgo nole ahani yitsasalidani sgu sgi nigalisdihv wininagvlvhvwunv yusdi wunigisv una wuninvno wuniyesdvna utloyuwu yegatli yvyesdvsgi sgu nunvnelv uniyesdvna
segments.translation: “I really think she was older than that,” I told my brother. “From what I heard, she was 114, they say,” he told me. There is a young man that lives right there. We talked the other day. “Have you seen that old lady they talk about?” he said to me. “Who, Jenny?” I said that. “How old she was ?” he told me. Then I went to Jay ‘couple days, and looked. Me and that young man that lives right there. He said: ”’Jenny Birdchopper--’ was written,” he said, “’--birthday 144 years old.’” “I believe it,” I told him. “I think it is true,” I told him. When she died, I was over there, we were talking. She had some flowers planted—just right there. She was fixing and cleaning them. ‘ She w at them. “I guess you all can do it now,” she told them. “But for now I am going in the house and rest,” she told them. I thought she was saying ‘just for now.’ “I am going to rest for now. You all stand here.” She went into the house. I was standing there, looking at them [the flowers]. And then my playmate came. “What are you looking at?” He said. “Jen was talking to those flowers she has planted there,” I told him. “All the time. Every day.” “But I am going into the house and rest,” she told them. I said to him, “She must have got tired.” “Let's go over to the water. There is two buckets, over there, we will get,” he told me. I said, “OK, five gallons.” “Five gallons full,” he had, setting. We got them and brought them up. And we set them there. The one they call Lol was cooking there. Ones name was Nvtsi. And then she said “You all eat. You all wake up Jen, we will eat,” or “You go give her something to eat. She has been working outside.” They could not wake her up. Her head was doing this [gestures]. They were doing this—they raised her arm—it would just hang down. They were rubbing her. “Jen is gone,” they said. “She is not doing anything. Lay her in the other bed.” When we did this, she went everywhere. She did not have any bones in her at all. When you did this [gestures] it bent all over and would raise and flop like this. They just rolled her up and got her and put her there. Laid her there just like laying a quilt down. That is how they did it. They laid her.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well I’ll be.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: “ᏚᏩᏃ ᎢᏛ” ᎤᏛᎾ ᎠᎬᏴᎳᏨᏃᏂ ᏍᎪᎯᏍᏆ ᏅᎩᏍᎯ ᏅᎩ Ꮕ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏗ ᎨᎮ ᏍᏈᏍᏛᏅ ᎨᏒ ᎡᎶ ᎡᎳᏗ ᎤᏪᏙᎴ ᏂᎦᏅᏛ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᏲ ᎤᎬᏴᎳᏣᏃᏅᏃ
segments.transliteration: “duwano idv” udvna agvyvlatsvnoni sgohisqua nvgishi nvgi nv yudetiyvdi gehe squisdvnv gesv elo eladi uwedole niganvdv sgina doyo ugvyvlatsanonvno
segments.translation: “She wilted,” they said. She just got too old. She was 144 years old. She walked a lot—everywhere on this earth, that one. She really just got too old.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎭ ᏥᏯᏅᏛᏗᏍᎪ ᏣᏗ ᎤᏪᏗ ᎤᎶᎩᎶ ᏥᏓᏳᎾᎷᏏᏗᏐ ᎩᏄᏗ ᏱᏓᏂᎳᏫᎦ ᎡᎳᏓ ᎦᏳᎳᏂ ᎤᎬᏴᎵᎨ ᏂᎨᏐ
segments.transliteration: yudaha tsiyanvdvdisgo tsadi uwedi ulogilo tsidayunalusidiso ginudi yidanilawiga elada gayulani ugvyvlige nigeso
segments.translation: I remember her at Old Cloud. You said she would be coming up. When they were having their quarterly church’. She would be walking. She was already an old lady.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.translation: Already was.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: She would be carrying a wood, doing this real slow.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: ᎾᏅ steps ᏥᏂᏙᎬᏅ ᎧᎶᏫᏛ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ. ᎣᏍᏗᏅ ᏍᎫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ. ᎤᎾᏅ ᏣᏂᏁᎸ ᏗᎦᏅᎪᎬᎾ ᎨᏂᏴ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎾ ᏧᎧᏂᎷᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏗᏝ ᎨᏛᎵ ᎣᎾᎾ ᏩᎬᏐᏛ ᎤᎾᏅ ᏩᎦᏐᏒᏍᎬ Ꭰ ᏫᎦᎶᏍᎪ ᏛᏳᏪᏴᎾ ᏫᎦᏕᏍᏓ ᎤᎾᎾ ᏙᎦᏥᏟᎪ Ꮓ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎢᎬᏅᎬᎵᏍᎪ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏍᎩ ᎾᏛᏁᎵᏍᎬ ᏃᎴ ᏳᏍᏆᏙᏂ ᏃᎴ ᏱᏓᎴᎲᎦ ᏱᏛᎦᏂᎷ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎫᏭᏂ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎰ ᎨᏛᏂᏒ. ᎾᏅ ᏅᏥ ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎰ ᎣᏂ ᎡᏙᎯ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎪᎯᏓ Ꮲ ᏗᏝ ᏱᏭᎶᏏ ᎣᏄᏛ Ꮲ ᏩᏁᏙᎰ ᏃᎴ ᏗᎦᏅᏅᎪᎪ ᏏᏫᏛ ᏢᏴ ᏄᏪᏒ ᎠᏯ ᎤᎬᏫᏴ ᎢᎦ ᏕᎦᏍᏓᏰᏍᎩ Ꮲ ᏬᏍᏕᏙᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏁᎵᎲᏂ ᎢᎦᏙᏩᏕᎪ ᎠᏗᎲ. ᏙᏳ ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎦᏗᏛ ᎾᏛᏁᎲ ᏭᏩᎦᏛᏅ ᎨᎲ ᏙᏳ ᏍᎫᏭᏂ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏩᏗ ᎡᏚᏗ ᏕᏃ ᏥᏕᏩᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꭽ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ ᏙᏯ ᏐᏁᎵ ᏍᎪᎯ ᏑᏓᎵ ᎠᏮᏓᏛᎦᏁᎸ ᎤᎾᏛᎾ Ꮎ ᏁᎲᏂ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᏜᏱᎪ ᏅᏴ ᏧᏪᎲᏃ ᎢᏤᏓᏍᏗ ᎠᏎ ᎨᏎ ᎤᎾ ᏥᎦᏁᎸ
segments.transliteration: nanv steps tsinidogvnv kalowidv yigohida. osdinv sgu tsigehv uwonihisdi. unanv tsaninelv diganvgogvna geniyv tsigehv una tsukanilusgi yusdi aditla gedvli onana wagvsodv unanv wagasosvsgv a wigalosgo dvyuweyvna wigadesda unana dogatsitligo no gusda osda igvnvgvlisgo nigada sgi nadvnelisgv nole yusquadoni nole yidalehvga yidvganilu gehv sguwuni nigalisdiho gedvnisv. nanv nvtsi tsitsiyoheho oni edohi gehv sgina gohida tlv ditla yiwulosi onudv tlv wanedoho nole diganvnvgogo siwidv tlvyv nuwesv aya ugvwiyv iga degasdayesgi tlv wosdedohv sgina gusdi nelihvni igadowadego adihv. doyu usquanigadidv nadvnehv wuwagadvnv gehv doyu sguwuni yiga awadi edudi deno tsidewasi tsigehv ha yawanvta doya soneli sgohi sudali awvdadvganelv unadvna na nehvni tsinulisdvnv dlayigo nvyv tsuwehvno itsedasdi ase gese una tsiganelv
segments.translation: And there were steps there, for how long. She could talk good, too. And where they lived, the spring was way over there, where it goes up ‘n then down in the hollow. And, there, she went down, and went way down that, towards the creek. And went around. She would be squatted down there. She would be cleaning something really good. She did things like that. When she was finished, she would get up and come back up. She would be using a stick for a cane. The one-I-call-Nvtsi would always follow. If she went somewhere, she would follow. They would go somewhere, then she would come out again. One day she said, “I am the one getting really tired when we go somewhere. And she don’t think nothing—walking around. It was amazing what she did.” And the rest of it? That’s all I know. Well, grandpa’s name? The late, Tsidewasi. I don’t know. Ninety-six—I heard they said, when he passed away. He lived in Jay. I guess you all went there, where he lived.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, uh-huh.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: ᎤᎾᎮᏂ ᏧᏭᏲᎱᏒ. ᏍᎫᏅ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᎾ ᏦᏍᏛᏓᏅᏟ ᎯᏂ ᏩᎦᏘᏲᏩᏕᎦ ᎤᎾ ᏍᎫ ᏪᏙᎲ ᎤᏪᏓᏍᏗ ᎨᏒ ᎤᎾᎾ ᏙᎩᎳᏫᏨ ᎤᎾ ᎠᏭ ᎤᎶᎩᎶ ᎤᎾᏂᎩᏌ ᎠᏥ Ꮕ ᎤᎵᏣᏙᏅ ᎾᏅ ᎤᏂᎷᏥᏃ. “ᏣᏚᏗᏛ ᏫᏰᏍᏛᎾ” ᎠᎪᏎᎸᏅ ᎾᎯᏳᏛ ᏌᎾᎴ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏛᏂ ᏱᏛᎵᏍᏓᏴᎲᎦ “ᎦᏳᎵ ᎮᏂ ᏥᏍᏓᏴᎲᎦ” ᎤᏛᏅ Ꮎ ᎠᎬᏴᎵᎨ ᏙᏅ ᏭᏴᏟ “ᎡᏚᏓ” ᎠᎪᎮᎴ “ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᎡᏍ ᏃᏭ.” Ꮂ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏳᏛᏁ ᏃᎴ ᎠᏥᏖᎸᏁ ᎤᏲᎱᏒ ᎡᎨᎮ. ᎤᏂᎩᏓ ᎦᏟᎲᏅ ᎬᏩᎦᏗ ᏭᏢᏁ. ᏙᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᎩᏄᏗ ᏙᎩᎳᏫᏨ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎤᎵᏍᏆᏝᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏭᏂᎷᏥ Ꮓ Ꮲ ᏱᏭᏰᏤ Ꮠ ᎢᎦ. ᏍᎫ Ꮫ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏓᏁᎦ ᏓᏳᏂᎶᏒ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎵ ᏐᎢ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᎤᎵᏍᎦᏂ ᏧᏙᎩᏗ ᏤᎲ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏟᏗᏝ ᏍᎫ ᎤᏛᏐᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ. segments.transliteration: unaheni tsuwuyohusv. sgunv utloyi nulisdvna tsosdvdanvtli hini wagatiyowadega una sgu wedohv uwedasdi gesv unana dogilawitsv una awu ulogilo unanigisa atsi nv ulitsadonv nanv unilutsino. “tsadudidv wiyesdvna” agoselvnv nahiyudv sanale yinulisdvni yidvlisdayvhvga “gayuli heni tsisdayvhvga” udvnv na agvyvlige donv wuyvtli “eduda” agohele “alisdadi es nowu.” hv gusdi yudvne nole atsitelvne uyohusv egehe. unigida gatlihvnv gvwagadi wutlvne. doheni squu ginudi dogilawitsv nahiyu ulisquatladi sgina wunilutsi no tlv yiwuyetse so iga. sgu dv nigalisdanega dayunilosv anigayvli soi heni squu ulisgani tsudogidi tsehv squu utliditla sgu udvsonv tsigehv. na e Cornshucker tsunadogida squunv utloyi nulisdvnv sgu gvwagatiwu unigisv sgu wutlvnv anadisgv aninohesgv M.D. tsanosehv hiyoliga nv gehe
segments.translation: He passed away there. And the same thing happened—my brother was watching him. He was over there. He used to go there all the time. We had church at Cloud, when they went home. Arch preached. And when they got back, “Go wake your grandpa up,” he told him that morning. “We eat: I cooked,” said the old lady. And when he went in, “Grandpa it is time to eat.” He didn’t say anything. He had passed away. He was gone while he was asleep. He went to sleep forever. We really did have our quarterly church then, the last time. And, when they got home, he didn’t wake up. It is going to happen like that—the elders are going to pass away. There is another that used to live on the other side. Ulisgvni was his name. He was an elder. Their names were Cornshucker. It happened the same way—he left forever. Went to sleep, they said, they were telling it—the one they called ‘MD’. I guess you knew him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: yeah

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: ᏗᎦᏂᏱᏍᎩ ᎢᎾ ᏏᎩᎵ ᎤᎾᏅ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏏᎩᎵ ᎨᎲ Ꭰ Colorado ᏗᏝ ᏧᏪᎲ ᎦᏳᎵ ᏐᎢᎾ Ꭰ Kansas city ᏫᎵ ᎠᏓᏬᏍᎩᏅ ᏃᎴ ᎠᏅ Ꭰ ᏙᏗ ᏣᏃᎮᎲ Oregon Ꮫ? Oregon ᏏᏛ ᏪᎰ ᎤᎾᎾ ᏙᏛ ᏧᏛᏗ ᎠᏎ ᏃᏫ ᏥᎦ. ᎠᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏗᏍᏆᎸᏍᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮠ ᏃᎴ Don ᏍᏊ ᎠᎾᏢᏅᏢ Don ᏧᏙᎩᏓ ᏤᎲ. ᎦᏁᏄᎵᏍᎦ ᏧᏓᎾᏥᏴ ᎤᎾᎾ. ᎨᎰᎩ ᏣᏂᏁᎸ ᎾᎾ ᏥᎬᏁᎸ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏠᏳ ᏍᎫ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᎾ ᏍᎫ ᎤᎬᏴᎳᏨᏭ ᏍᎫ ᏢᏍᎩᏂ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏗ ᎨᎲ Ꮓ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏔᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᏊ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏭᏅᎦᏛ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏯᏭ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏥᎦ Ꮓ ᏦᎦᏛᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏦᎩᏙᏓ ᏦᎩᎵᏌᏅ ᏦᎩᏥ Ꮥ ᎹᎹ ᎮᏂ ᏝᎦ ᎣᏏ ᏧᎴᏂᏙᎸ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏧᏂᎩᏒ Ꮓ ᎠᏫ ᎯᎢ ᏃᎴ ᎣᎩᏥᏫ ᏱᎦ Ꮓ ᏄᏛᎾᏕᎬ ᎠᏫ. ᎠᎮᏂ ᏗᎧᏃᎩᏏᏙ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎫ ᎠᎨᏯ. ᎣᏥᏰᏣᏙᏗ ᏃᎴ ᎺᎵᎾ ᎠᏰᏣᏓᏂᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏍᎫ Ꮫ ᏄᏍᏗᏓᏅ ᏦᎩᎶᏏ
segments.transliteration: diganiyisgi ina sigili unanv aseno sigili gehv a Colorado ditla tsuwehv gayuli soina a Kansas city wili adawosginv nole anv a dodi tsanohehv Oregon dv? Oregon sidv weho unana dodv tsudvdi ase nowi tsiga. ada heni disqualvsga tsigehv so nole Don squu anatlvnvtlv Don tsudogida tsehv. ganenulisga tsudanatsiyv unana. gehogi tsaninelv nana tsigvnelv squu utloyu sgu yusdi nulisdvna sgu ugvyvlatsvwu sgu tlvsgini yawanvti yudetiyvdi gehv no sgina utani tsigehv squu nowunv wunvgadv gehv ayawu yawadetiyvda tsiga no tsogadvsv sgina tsogidoda tsogilisanv tsogitsi de mama heni tlaga osi tsulenidolv edoda tsunigisv no awi hii nole ogitsiwi yiga no nudvnadegv awi. aheni dikanogisido gehv sgu ageya. otsiyetsadodi nole melina ayetsadanido tsigehv. sgu dv nusdidanv tsogilosi
segments.translation: Diganiyisgi Sigil, but Sigil lived towards Colorado. Another one lives in Kansas City, Wili. And ᎠᏓᏬᏍᎩ How do they say Oregon? He still lives there. I guess he is wealthy now. He was a wood cutter. And, another one, Tom. That was his sibling. Tom was his name, that lived there. Gvnenulisgi was a son in-law, there. Married to Kehogi. He lived there, too. It's just like the same thing happened to him, too—he just got old. I don’t know how old that one was. He was older, too. And the rest of them, we are about the same age, we brought them up. Our dads, our grandmas, I mean [raised them]. Our mom, too. She was good. But then Dad left there. Just our mom was around there. But she was a singing woman, we would laugh at her too. Mel used to laugh at her. That’s the way it was—how we came.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎾᎭ Ꮎ ᏥᏍᎩᏃᏎᎲ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏗ ᎠᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎩ ᏤᎮ ᎯᏗᏝ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᎠᏫ ᎠᎹᏯ ᏗᎦᎾᏗᏒ Ꮓ ᏩᏴᎯᎲ
segments.transliteration: nanaha na tsisginosehv sawu yuwagadi alitsidohvsgi tsehe hiditla tsadihv. awi amaya diganadisv no wayvhihv
segments.translation: What about that one time? You were telling me there was a preacher that lived across the water farther in?

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.translation: It was Jack.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So it was Jack.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: ᏤᎦ ᏧᏙᎩᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎹᎹ ᎤᏥ--ᎤᏙᏓ. ᎤᎾ Ꮫ ᏛᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᎤᎨᏓᎵᏴ ᏭᏅᎪᏟᏢ ᏭᎨᏛᎵᏴ ᏓᎦᎶᏍᎬ ᏃᎴᏅ ᏓᎧᎾᎷᏍᎬ ᎠᎨ ᎠᏰᏟᏴ Ꮲ ᎠᏂᎩᏓ ᏭᏅᏓᏟ ᎯᏗᏝ ᏓᏕᏘᏂᎯ ᎤᎾᎾ ᎬᏅᏅ ᏃᏫᏥᎦ church Ꭲ ᎤᎾ ᎠᏫᏴ ᎠᎦᏐᏏᎯ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᏅᏂ ᎯᎾ ᎤᎾᏅ ᎠᏫᏴ ᎠᎦᏐᏏᎯ
segments.transliteration: tsega tsudogida tsigehv na mama utsi--udoda. una dv dvnigisgv ugedaliyv wunvgotlitlv wugedvliyv dagalosgv nolenv dakanalusgv age ayetliyv tlv anigida wunvdatli hiditla dadetinihi unana gvnvnv nowitsiga church i una awiyv agasosihi sgina ganvni hina unanv awiyv agasosihi
segments.translation: It was Jack. Jack was his name—he was Mama’s mom— [I mean,] her dad. He would come from the hollow, where it came out. Where it went to the hollow. And then he came back up, way over there. About halfway there is a ridge place. He would come out there, where the church is now. There was a road. It comes down close to there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: The old Cloud Creek?

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: ᎥᎲ. ᎤᎾᏅ ᎤᎨᏛᎵᏴ ᏳᏣᎶᏏ ᎯᏗᏝ ᎤᎾ ᎦᏚᏏᏴ ᎠᏕᏘᏂᎯ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎡᏍᎦ ᏱᏗᎦᎶᏏ ᎯᏗᏝ ᎤᎾᎾ ᏗᎦᎶᏍᎩ. ᏓᏓᎾᏫᏍᏗ ᏃᎴ Ꭸ ᏥᎧᎾᎷᏍᎩ ᏯᏖᏂ ᏅᏃ ᎤᎾ ᎤᏅᏓᏝ ᏓᏓᎾᏫᏍᏗ ᎤᎾᎾ ᎤᎾᏅ ᏙᏗᎦᏅᏗᏩᏍᎬ. ᎠᏭᏅ ᎦᏚᏌ ᎯᏗᏝ ᎥᎦᏓ ᏄᏍᏓ ᏃᎴ ᏗᎠᎦᏐᏍᎩ ᎯᏗᏝ ᎥᎦᏓ ᎠᏩ ᎨᏥᏗᏓᏁᎳ ᎤᎾᏭ ᎤᏟᏗᏢ ᎠᏕᏘᏂᎯ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎯᏗᏝᎥᎦᏔ ᏫᏂᎬᎾ ᎤᎾᏅ ᏓᎬᎶᏍᎬ ᎤᎾ ᏙᎬᏂᏗᏍᎬ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏫᏙᎦᏐᎬᏂ ᎠᎹᏯ ᎠᏩᎩ ᎤᎾ ᎤᎨᏛᎵᏴ ᏩᏴᎯᎥ ᎠᎭᏂᏴ ᎤᏂᎩᏓ ᎥᎧᏂᎷᏍᎬ ᏃᎴ ᎤᏔᏂ ᎠᏔᎴᏏ ᎤᎾᎾ cave ᎤᎾᏅ ᏩᏴᎯᎲ piney church ᎯᏗᏝ ᏥᏦᏓᎳ ᎤᎾ ᏫᎬᏅᎪᎬ cave ᏫᎦᎶᏍᎬ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ᎤᏩᏅᏕᏍᎬ ᎤᎾ ᏳᏭᎷᏥ ᏫᏙᎦᏐᎬ ᎠᎹᏯ ᎤᎾ church ᏫᎦᎷᎬ
segments.transliteration: vhv. unanv ugedvliyv yutsalosi hiditla una gadusiyv adetinihi nowunv esga yidigalosi hiditla unana digalosgi. dadanawisdi nole ge tsikanalusgi yateni nvno una unvdatla dadanawisdi unana unanv dodiganvdiwasgv. awunv gadusa hiditla vgada nusda nole diagasosgi hiditla vgada awa getsididanela unawu utliditlv adetinihi sgina hiditlavgata winigvna unanv dagvlosgv una dogvnidisgv ahani widogasogvni amaya awagi una ugedvliyv wayvhiv ahaniyv unigida vkanilusgv nole utani atalesi unana cave unanv wayvhihv piney church hiditla tsitsodala una wigvnvgogv cave wigalosgv sgi yigohida uwanvdesgv una yuwulutsi widogasogv amaya una church wigalugv
segments.translation: Yeah, and if you go up the hollow, it's like this—it comes out way on top. It comes, then it comes back this way. And that’s how he came. There is a crossroad, over there. Where it goes up a wide road. It’s a ridge—there is a crossroad. He came across there. And, over there, on the hill, it's like this. And it comes down, this way, where that building is—beside. It comes out, just on the other side. It goes that way. He came across. Then, he went across the water and went back into the hollow. He would go a little way and went back up. There is a big hole there—a cave, and he would go in there. Where Piney Church is [beside Beaty Creek, Jay]—the mountain on this side. He came out there. He went, through the cave, for that long it was level, when he got there. He would cross the water and get to the church.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎭᎳᎩ ᏳᏟᎶᏗ ᏴᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ? ᏳᏩᏴᏟ ᎤᎾ
segments.transliteration: halagi yutlilodi yvda sgina? yuwayvtli una
segments.translation: How many miles would you say that is?

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏗ ᏑᏟᎶᏗ Ꮲ ᏴᏗ ᏳᎪᏗᏭ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏍᏗ Ꮶ ᎩᏄᏗ ᎴᏢ ᏱᎦ
segments.transliteration: asedi sutlilodi tlv yvdi yugodiwu leyiga sdi tso ginudi letlv yiga
segments.translation: I think it is about half a mile, you would say. It might be more, just a little. Might be about a quarter [more].

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So he would walk that long, in that hole?

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: ᎥᎲ ᏯᏖᏂ Ꮫ ᎠᏗᎲ Ꭸ ᏱᎦᏗ. ᎤᎾᏅ ᏂᏛᏳᏅᎪᏍᏗ Ꭰ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏂᎬᏅ ᏯᏙᏟᏭ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᎦᏅᎪᎬ Ꮓ ᏙᎮᏂ ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏗ Ꮩ ᎠᏪᏙᎸᎮᏂ ᏩᎩᏴᏢ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏗ ᎠᏎᎾ Ꭰ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᏥᏍᎪᎵ ᏛᎥᏩᎦᏛᎭᏒ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏄᏍᏗᏓᏅ ᎯᏅ ᏛᎬᎶᏍᎬ Ꮫ ᏒᏃᏱ ᎠᏨᏯᏍᏗᏅ ᎪᎯᏅᏍᏗ ᎬᏗᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏨᏯᏍᏛᏍᎬ Ꮓ ᏧᏄᎪᏣᏭ church Ꭲ ᏙᏗᎦᏐᎬ ᏕᎦᏃᎱᎩᏍᎬᏂ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏗ ᎤᎾ ᏚᏢᏅ ᎯᏄᏍᏛ ᏚᏄᏩ ᏙᏗᎤᏩᏐᏨᎾ ᏧᏚᎩᏏᏅ ᏃᎴ ᏚᏄᏬᎥ ᏃᎴ ᏗᎤᎾᎷᏎ. ᎤᎾ ᏗᎤᏴᏞ ᎤᎾ ᎤᎨᏛᎵᏴᎤᎾᏅ ᏗᎤᏅᎪᏤ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏃᎴ ᏚᏩᏐᏤᏃ ᏃᎴ Ꭰ ᏭᏕᎵᏤ ᎦᏚᏌ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏒᏃᏱ Ꮲ ᎢᎦᎾᏅᎪᎪ. ᎤᎶᎲᏍᏗ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏒᏃᏱ ᏌᏭ ᎤᏩᏂᎸ Ꮲ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏄᏛᏅᏕᎬ ᏕᎦᎳᏫᏥᏙᎲ ᏙᏳ Ꭷ ᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᏍᏓᏲᏒ Ꭷ ᎤᏬᎯᏳ ᎨᏎ ᎨᎵᎰ ᎪᎯᏅ ᏥᎦ ᏱᎩᎲᏲᎵᎦ ᏍᎫ ᎭᎵᏱᎦ ᏍᏓᏯ ᏳᏂᎨᏌ ᏳᏩᎩᎵᏬᏤᏛ ᎠᏫᏢ ᏱᏓᏗᏛ ᏃᎴ ᏙᏳᏛ
segments.transliteration: vhv yateni dv adihv ge yigadi. unanv nidvyunvgosdi a yusdi nigvnv yadotliwu yusdi diganvgogv no doheni sgi nusdi do awedolvheni wagiyvtlv heni sdi asena a nulisdvnv tsisgoli dvvwagadvhasv. sgina nusdidanv hinv dvgvlosgv dv svnoyi atsvyasdinv gohinvsdi gvdiho sgina atsvyasdvsgv no tsunugotsawu church i dodigasogv deganohugisgvni sawu yuwagadi una dutlvnv hinusdv dunuwa dodiuwasotsvna tsudugisinv nole dunuwov nole diunaluse. una diuyvtle una ugedvliyvunanv diunvgotse ahani nole duwasotseno nole a wudelitse gadusa sgina svnoyi tlv igananvgogo. ulohvsdi leyiga svnoyi sawu uwanilv tlv sgidv nudvnvdegv degalawitsidohv doyu ka gelisgo sdayosv ka uwohiyu gese geliho gohinv tsiga yigihvyoliga sgu haliyiga sdaya yunigesa yuwagiliwotsedv awitlv yidadidv nole doyudv
segments.translation: He said it was wide for a long ways. And where it came out it was, like this—kind of narrow. Then it came out. It was really like that. I have been there. I have been in there a little ways, but my head went like this [gestures meeting the cave ceiling]. I turned back. That’s what happened. He would come through there. At night time he would be using a light-you-carry. He would light it up. When he would come out of church, he would come across. It was flooding one time. He laid his clothes here [gesturing], and came across. When got out, he put them back on. He came up and went back in the hollow. He came back out, and crossed again, on foot. Then he dove up the hill. He would come out at dark, or way past dark—around one [o’clock]. That’s the way he was going to church. I really think he was a strong believer. Now’days we would get lazy. Even if your car has a hard time starting, “It might die out,” we will say. Really.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I remember, too. They would be carrying lights.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s the way they were.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You could only see with those lights, I remember.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏗ ᎠᏮᏌ ᏃᎯᎢ ᎠᏩᎨ Ꮕ ᏦᏥᏁᎸ Ꮎ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏗᏓᏁᎸ ᎨᎲ ranch Ꭲ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎾ ᏬᏥᏁᎸ ᎺᎵ Ꮫ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎤᏍᏗᏭ Ᏼ ᏂᎦᏛ ᎩᎳ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎡᏙ ᎣᏍᏗ Ꮥ ᎡᏙᎯ ᎨᎲ ᏐᎢᎾ ᎤᏔᏅ corina ᎠᏯᏅ ᎠᏥ ᏦᎩᎾᏛᏂ. ᎣᏥᏅ ᎡᏙᏗᎾ ᎦᏃᎲᎵᏙ ᎨᎲ ᏂᎪᎸ ᏒᏃᏱ. ᎩᏝ ᏚᏛᏓᏍᏗᏕᎪ ᏚᎾᏝᎥ ᏗᏂᎨᎯᏙ ᏩᏯ ᏃᎴ ᏧᏟ ᏚᏛᏓᏍᏗᏕᎪ ᎠᏫ ᎦᏚᏏ ᎠᏥ ᎤᎾᎵᎪ ᎤᎾ ᏚᏃᏢ ᎤᎵᏏᎦ ᎨᎲ ᏃᏭᏂ ᎡᎾᎨ ᏛᎨᏏ ᎪᏩᏒ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎤᎾᏤᎵᏍᏗ Ꭸ ᏙᏛᏣᏯᎴᏏ? ᎡᎵᏭ ᏱᏙᏛᏥᏅᏍᏗ ᏱᏗᎦᎢ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ. ᎰᏩ ᏣᏓᎦᏎᏍᏕᏍᏗ ᏗᎾ ᎰᏩ ᎠᏨᏍᏗ ᎪᎢᏁᎮᏍᏗ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ. ᎰᏩ ᎩᏟ Ꮫ ᎠᏫ ᏕᎨᎵᏒᏗ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏱᏛᏘᎾᏫᏛᎯ ᎠᏂᎬᏴᎵ Ꮲ ᎤᏟᏱᎦ ᏳᎨᎬᏥᏘᏃᎩ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎠᏬᎮᎸ. ᏗᎬᎦᎢᏐ ᏛᎩᎾᎷᏒ ᎤᎾᎾ Ꮓ ᏧᏅᏓᏝᎲ ᏛᎦᎢᏒ Ꭸ ᎠᏰᏟ ᏓᏓᎾᏫᏍᏛ ᏥᎬᏗᏍᎬ ᎤᎾ Ꮲ ᎠᏩᎴᏫᏍᏛᏅ. ᏃᏫᏛ ᎤᎾᏗᎦᎴᏲᏨ ᎩᏟ ᎤᎾᏛ ᏙᏗᏳᎾᏑᏫᏒ Ꭸ ᏃᏫᏛ ᎠᎭᏂᏭ ᏛᎮ ᏯᏬᏟ ᎠᏪᎵᏒ ᏡᎦ ᎤᎾᏅᏂᏓᏍᏗ ᏚᏃᏢᏒ ᎤᎾ ᏩᏮᎵᏍᏛᏡᏅ ᎤᎾ ᏥᎦᎰ ᎦᏥᏯᏛᏓᏍᏙ. ᎾᏍᎩᏂ ᎯᏗᏝ ᏂᏛᏁ ᎯᏗᏝ ᏭᏅᏕᎵᏨ ᎡᏝᏪ ᏫᏄᎾᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᎯᏗᏝ ᎡᎵᏭᏕ ᏩᏯ ᏯᏂᏩᏘ ᎠᏪᎵᏒ. ᎠᏩᎨ ᎾᏂᎨᏍᏗ ᏫᏛᏥᎷᏥ ᎠᏪᎵᏒ ᏓᏩᎴᏅ Ꮓ ᏛᎥᏩᏂᎩᏒ ᎤᎾ Ꮲ ᎦᏚᏏ ᎠᏩᎴᏫᏍᏛᏅ ᎤᎾ ᎣᏍᏛ ᎤᎾᎾ ᎠᏩᎵᏍᏛᏡᏅ. ᎤᎾ ᎠᏬᏢ ᎠᏨᏍᏛ ᏗᏍ ᎤᎴᏅᎲ ᎡᎳᏓ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲ ᎠᎢ ᎤᏴᏟ ᏩᏩᏒᏁᎸ ᎤᎵᏏᎦ Ꮫ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ Ꮓ ᎠᏎᏗ ᎠᎭᏂᏭ ᎠᏬᏞᏍᏗ ᎠᏬᏘᏅ ᎠᏭ ᎠᏪᎵᏒ. ᎠᎭᏂᏃ ᎠᏬᏞᏍᏗ ᎠᏪᎵᎲ ᏃᎴ ᎠᏂᎨᎯᏙᎲ ᎠᏫᏴ ᎠᏂᎶᏍᎪ ᎪᎯᏴ ᎤᏂᎷᏨ Ꮓ. ᎡᏥᏂᏱᏧ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎤᎾᎾᏢᏂᏙᎸ ᎠᏫᏴ ᏙᏍᎫᏃ ᎠᏩᏟᏴᎩᏓᏁᎰ ᎤᎵᏏᎦ Ꮓ ᎨᎲ ᎨᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎸᎯᏳ ᎣᎨᏙᎸ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎤᎾᏴ ᎨᏙᎲ ᎣᏍᏓᏅ ᎦᏅᏅ. ᏙᎲᏃ ᏛᎬᏛᏁᎵ ᎨᎵᎰ ᎠᏩᏗᏍ ᎥᎬᏃᎯᎵᏒ ᎤᏥᏍᏓᎷᎦ ᏥᏂᏴᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᏘᏍᏗᎲ Ꭰ ᎾᏮᏅ ᏮᏥᏂᏕᏒ ᎠᏥᏯᏴᎸᏅ ᏃᎴ ᏐᎢ ᎬᏩᏍᏚᏭᏛ ᎢᏂᏅᎪᏨᏃ ᏕᎦᏥᏂᏱᎲ ᏓᏩᏄᏩ ᏃᎴ ᏓᏮᏁᎸ ᏃᎴ ᏗᏥᏍᏆᎨᏂ ᏗᏝ Ꮓ ᎣᏍᏗ ᎡᎦ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᏃᏫᏛ ᏩᏩᏂᎩᏒ ᏫᏥᏍᏓᏩᏛᏒ ᏅᏃ ᎣᏍᏗ Ꮫ ᎬᏂ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏫ ᏳᏍᏗ. ᎨᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏱᏗᎦᏠᏍᎨ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎮᏂ ᎡᎦ ᏚᏨᏍᏛ ᏍᎫᏛ ᏚᏍᏗᏕᎬ ᎠᎠᎠ ᏩᎩᎦᏐᏒ ᏩᎩᎷᏨ ᏓᏁᎸ. ᏙᏳ ᎬᎵᎡᎵᏥᏍᎢ ᏍᏆᏁᏝᏅ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ

segments.translation: One time, this is myself—over there, where we lived. That good house, it was a ranch. We lived there. Mel was little, just little, about yea tall [gestures]. ‘Just now walking good, or she was walking good. The other was bigger. Corene, me, and Arch were adults. We were sitting there. And dad used to hunt all the time. At night time he would be listening, to the dogs he had, that chased coyotes and foxes. He would be listening—Arch and him. They were sitting there, it was dark. “I am going to the woods tonight,” I told him. “Are you going to look for possums?” “I might bring some when I am coming back,” I told him. “OK, watch yourself.” “OK, I will be carrying a light.” I told him. “Ok. ‘Dogs are tied up right there. Take them. They are old, they will not take you very far away.” He told me. I kept walking and came on up. I was walking on a ridge over there. About halfway, where I said, there was a crossroad. About there, I stopped, and the dogs scattered out. They barked way over there. So, I thought “I will just sit right here, at this tree.” There were some places to sit, so I sat down. I was sitting there, listening. When they came up they went that way. They got quite far that way. They might have found a coyote, I thought. I am going to get closer, I thought. And I got up, and I started walking. Somewhere on top I stopped, and I sat down. I was sitting there and the light started getting low. I ran out of coal oil. It got dark. “I guess I am just going to sit here. I have a fire,” I thought. “I am just going to sit here.” They were chasing just over there. They went by, and came back. I said “Did you all catch it?” They just laid down. I was really getting suspicious. It was dark now. We had never been that far. Where I was, there was a good road. I thought “What am I going to do now?” There was a lightning bug flying right there, I caught it. It was shining good light when I held it, and I took its tail off. I stuck it on [my clothes] and then another—they started coming out. I was catching them, putting them on my clothes, and then it was kind of light. Then I started walking. I followed the road. It was clear, right there—they were not going dim. It was good light. That was the way it was. I went off and got back to the house. “I really appreciate you, my God,” I told Him.

segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏓᎩᎾᏅᎪᏫᏎᎸ Ꮎ ᎠᎩᎪᏩᏛᏗ ᎠᏩᏂᎩᏍᏓ. ᏙᏳ ᎬᎵᎡᎵᏥᏍ ᏍᏆᏁᏢᏅ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ Ꮲ ᎸᏢ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎠᏩᏓᏖᏗ ᏱᎬᎩᎪᎮ ᏂᎯ ᏂᎨᏒᏂ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏥᏲᎮᎸᏂ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩᎾᏅᎪᏫᏎᎸ. ᎤᏬᏢ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏓ ᏩᎩᏴᏟᏝ. ᎦᎵᏕ ᎥᎯᎷᎩ ᎤᎾ ᏫᏛᏥᎶᏏᏒ ᎩᎳᏫ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏧᏛᏅ ᏓᏪᎷᎯᎢᎨᏅ. ᎣᏍᏛ ᎾᏩᏛᏅᏕᎬ ᎨᏴ ᏭᎵᏍᏛ ᏬᏤᏗ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎤᎾ ᏣᏂᎨᎯᏙᎲ ᏭᎵᏍᏛ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎯᏗᏝ Ꮲ ᏥᎾᏂᎶᏍᎬ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏃᎴ Hubert Ꭲ ᏗᏝ. O ᎨᏍᏗ Ꮫ ᏱᎦᏥᏯᏛᎩᏍᎨ ᎠᏗᎲ. ᏓᎦᏥᏴᎸᏏ ᎨᎵᎲ ᎮᏂᏃ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎮᏂ. ᎤᎾ ᏬᎩᎷᏨ ᎾᎾ ᎬᎵᎡᎵᎩ ᏗᎾ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏫᏕᏓ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏌᎾᎴ ᎢᏨᏰᎶᎸᎢ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ Ꮓ ᎣᎩᏒᏢ ᎣᏂ ᏃᏭ ᎨᏒ ᎠᎹᏯ ᏭᏛ ᏂᎦ ᏂᎬ ᎨᏙᎲ Ꮓ ᏛᏳᎶᏒ ᏥᏍᏛᏂ Ꮽ ᏕᏥᏘᏟᏙᎲ ᏍᎫᏛ ᏢᎫᏍᏗ ᏄᏓᎴ ᎤᏨᏘᎾ ᎡᎵᏕᎰᏂ ᏱᎦ ᏗᎨᏛᏍᏗ ᏍᎫ Ꮫ ᏂᎦᎥ ᏙᏦᏢᏍᎬ Ꮎ. ᎠᏥ ᎢᎾ Ꮲ ᏗᎦᏙᎪ ᏙᏗᎦᏟᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᏚᏢᎰᏂ ᏫᏙᏥᎾᏕᎪ ᏃᎴ ᎣᎬᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᎣᎩᏩᏍᎪ ᏃᎴ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎣᏣᎵᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎪ ᏒᎯᏰ ᏍᎫ ᏃᏨᏛᏁᎲ ᎤᏙᏙᏩᏗ. ᎫᏍᏗᏭ ᏗᏗᏍᏗ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏓᏲᏢᏍᎪ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏓ Ꮲ ᏲᎩᏍᏆᎵᏏ ᏱᎦ ᏌᏭ ᎢᏥᏲ ᎠᏲᏢᏍᎪ ᏃᎴ ᏳᏝᏅᏛᏕᎵ ᏃᎴ Ꮲ ᏗᏝ ᏫᎠᎢᏐ ᏐᎢ ᏩᏲᏢᏍᎪ. ᏍᎩᏃ ᏂᎦᏗ ᏱᏚᏲᏢᏃᏂ ᏐᏈᎳ ᎢᏥᏯᏘᏁᎪ ᎠᏯ. ᏙᏥᏳᏛᎸᏁᎰ ᏃᏭ ᏙᏍᏗᏟᏏᎰ ᎦᎸᎾᏗ truck ᎬᏪᏓᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏙᏍᏗᏗᏍᎬ ᎾᏅ ᎤᎨᏛᎵᏴ ᎮᏂ ᏙᏍᏗᏱᏍᎬ ᏙᏍᏗᏅᏟᏗᎲ ᎠᏥᏅ ᏍᎩᏛᏅ ᎦᎾᏅᎪᏥᏙᎰ ᏗᎨᏛᏍᏗ ᏙᏗᏲᏢᏍᎪᏢ Ꮲ ᎣᏍᏗᏛ ᏃᎬᏛᏅᏕᎬ ᏏᏆ Ꮕ ᏙᏥᎯᎰ ᏃᎴ ᏓᎵᏗᏍᏗᎰ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏓ. ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏃᎴ ᎣᎬᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᎣᎩᎰ ᎢᏌ ᏄᎾ, ᏚᏯ ᏙᎩᏩᏍᎪ Ꮎ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏛᏅ ᎢᎦ ᎣᏣᎵᏍᏓᏂᏙᎰ ᎣᏣᎢᏒ ᎮᏍᏛ ᎠᎪᏂ ᏱᏃᎬᏛᏁ. ᎪᎯᏅ ᏥᎦ ᏄᏛᎴ ᏄᏍᏓ

O gesdi dv yigatsiyadvgisge adihv. dagatsiyvlvsi gelihv henino tsadihv heni. una wogilutsv nana gvlieligi dina gatsiyohelv osda wideda gatsiyohelv sanale itsvyelolvi gatsiyohelv no ogisvtlv oni nowu gesv amaya wudv niga nigv gedohv no dvyulosv tsisdvni wu detsititlidohv sgudv tlvgusdi nudale utsvtina elidehoni yiga digedvsdi sgu dv nigav dotsotlvsgv na. atsi ina tlv digadogo dodigatliho sgina yidutlvhoni widotsinadego nole ogvlisdadi ogiwasgo nole osda otsalisdayvhvsgo svhiye sgu notsvdvnehv udodowadi. gusdiwu didisdi leyiga dayotlvsgo udvhisda tlv yogisqualisi yiga sawu itsiyo ayotlvsgo nole yutlanvdvdeli nole tlv ditla wiaiso soi wayotlvsgo. sgino nigadi yiduyotlvnoni soquila itsiyatinego aya. dotsiyudvlvneho nowu dosditlisiho galvnadi truck gvwedasdi gehv dosdidisgv nanv ugedvliyv heni dosdiyisgv dosdinvtlidihv atsinv sgidvnv gananvgotsidoho digedvsdi dodiyotlvsgotlv tlv osdidv nogvdvnvdegv siqua nv dotsihiho nole dalidisdiho udvhisda. sginana nole ogvlisdadi ogiho isa nuna, duya dogiwasgo na osda dvnv iga otsalisdanidoho otsaisv hesdv agoni yinogvdvne. gohinv tsiga nudvle nusda
segments.translation: He gave me those to see, to go home with. “I really appreciate you. my God,” I told Him. “I would not have seen anything to think about, if it was not for you,” I told Him. He revealed that to me. The old man was sitting there when I came in. “Are you already back? I was going to go that way, in a little bit,” he said. He was concerned for me. I was doing good. “We went way over there, to the end.” I told him. “They were really chasing. They would go this way,” I told him. ”And then that way.” “Oh, I didn’t hear them,” he said. “I was thinking I better go look for them.” When we got back, I told them I was thankful we had a good time. “I will feed you tomorrow.” I told them. We went to sleep. And then—toward the last—I was going everywhere in the creek. Gigging crawdads [with a small gig spear]. That was it—nothing, nowhere else. Sometimes we made fence posts. Arch would be standing somewhere, sharpening them. And, when he would sharpen them, we would sell them and buy food. We would eat good in the evening. That is what we did all day. Or something. Or the old man would carve railroad ties. If we cut one somewhere, it would be laying there. He would carve it, when he got time. Then he would walk somewhere else, and carve another one. And when he would carve all of them, I would take a horse. I would hook them on, ‘gather them together, and take them up to where a truck would go. We would load them up. We would get them out of the hollow—we would haul them up. Arch would be going around carving posts somewhere. We were doing good. We would kill a hog. Dad would fatten them up, and then we would have food. Just flour, potatoes, and beans—we would buy that. And then we would be eating good. We were not starving. Now’days it is different.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah it's different.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: ᎠᏥᏃᏅ four days ᏳᏍᏆᎸ ᏬᏤᏙᎰ ᏂᎪᎸ truck ᎤᏛ ᎣᎦᏦᏗ ᎠᎩᏩᎶᎢᏐ ᎣᎾᏗᏢ ᏃᎴ ᎠᏓ ᏙᏥᏍᏆᎵᏍᎪ ᎡᎾᎨ ᏬᏥᏴᎯᎰ ᏙᏥᎾᏗᏍᎪ highway ᎯᏗᏝ ᏧᎶᏟᎩ ᏥᏝᏗᏍᏗᎰ ᎤᎾᎾ ᏥᏳᎦᏚᏩ ᏂᎴ ᏗᎦᎵᏦᏗ ᏙᏥᏢᏍᎪ. ᎡᎳᏗᏭ Ꮕ Ᏼ ᏗᎦᏗ ᏙᏤᏛᏍᎪ ᎠᏍᏛ ᎠᏂᏅ ᏙᏥᎾᎸᏗᎰ Ꮠ ᎣᏍᏗᏛ ᎣᏥᏴᎯᎰ Ꮓ ᎤᎾᎾ ᎣᎩᏒᏟᏓᏍᏗ ᏅᎩᎭ ᏧᏒᎯᏓ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏃᎬᏛᏅᏕᎦ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏲᎨᏂ ᎤᎾᎾ ᎤᎾ Ꮫ ᏬᏤᏙᎰ ᏅᎩᎭ ᏧᏒᎯᏓ ᎤᎾᏭ ᎠᏐᏴ ᎤᏟᏗᏢ ᏫᏙᏥᏗᏍᎪ Ꮎ pole ᎨᎲ ᏙᏥᏲᏭ Ꮟ ᏑᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏳᏬᎨᏙᎵ
segments.transliteration: atsinonv four days yusqualv wotsedoho nigolv truck udv ogatsodi agiwaloiso onaditlv nole ada dotsisqualisgo enage wotsiyvhiho dotsinadisgo highway hiditla tsulotligi tsitladisdiho unana tsiyugaduwa nile digalitsodi dotsitlvsgo. eladiwu nv yv digadi dotsedvsgo asdv aninv dotsinalvdiho so osdidv otsiyvhiho no unana ogisvtlidasdi nvgiha tsusvhida. sgina nogvdvnvdega nigohilv yogeni unana una dv wotsedoho nvgiha tsusvhida unawu asoyv utliditlv widotsidisgo na pole gehv dotsiyowu si sudetiyvda yuwogedoli
segments.translation: At Cedar Tree, when they had a four day event, we went all the time. In a Buick. I would be bouncing around in the back. Then we would cut wood. We would go in the woods across the highway. It split this way [gestures]. I would lay it across straight, then we would cut shingles. Then we would stand posts low. Yea tall [gestures] on the sides. We would put across on one side. It was good. Then we would go in there to sleep. Four nights [we stayed]. That is what we used to do, all the time, when we would go there. When we went there—four nights. We would lay the posts next to the fence. They would be laying there when we went back the next year.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Laying there.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, ᏃᎴ ᏫᏙᏥᏱᎰ ᏫᏙᏥᏝᏗᎰ ᎡᎦᏓ ᏧᏪᏘ ᎨᎰ ᏓᏲᎪ ᏃᎴ ᎢᏤ ᏬᏥᏱᎰ ᏍᎫ ᏃᏣᏛᏁᎰ
segments.transliteration: vhv, nole widotsiyiho widotsitladiho egada tsuweti geho dayogo nole itse wotsiyiho sgu notsadvneho
segments.translation: We would get them, and lay them across. Some were too old, They would break. Then we would go get a new one. We just did that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎯᏳ ᏛᎭ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᏈᏍᏓ ᏥᎾᎾᎵᏍᏗᎰ ᏅᎩ ᏧᏙᏛᏩᏗ ᏣᏁᏙᎰ
segments.transliteration: nahiyu dvha tsigehv squisda tsinanalisdiho nvgi tsudodvwadi tsanedoho
segments.translation: Back then there would be lots of people that would come for four days.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.translation: ’Was a lot.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᏣᎩᏍᏗᎬ ᏍᎫ ᏬᎨᏓᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎤᎾ ᏧᏓᎴᏅᏗ ᏗᎪᏩᏛᏗ ᏥᎨᎰ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ ᎤᎾ ᏂᎬᏭ ᏗᏁ ᏗᎪᏩᏛᏗ
segments.transliteration: aya heni squu tsagisdigv sgu wogedasdi gehv una tsudalenvdi digowadvdi tsigeho anitsalagi una nigvwu dine digowadvdi
segments.translation: When I was little we used to go there. Yeah, you would see a lot of different Cherokee people. From other places—you would see [them].

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: ᏍᎨ, ᏙᏥᏃᎩᏍᎪᏅ ᏃᎴ ᏓᏂᏃᎩᏍᎪ Ꮥ ᏙᏛᏫᏕᏂ ᎤᏒ ᎤᎵᏨᏛᏩᏗ ᏳᎾᏚᎵ. ᏅᎩ ᎤᏩᏂᎸ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᏙᏥᏃᎩᏍᎪ ᏳᏩᏪᏙᎵ ᏳᏬᎩᏴᏟ. ᎠᏥ ᎢᏛ ᏙᏳ ᏍᏈᏍᏓ ᏗᎧᏂᎩᏍᏓ ᏚᏅᏛ. ᏙᎦᏖ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎮᏂ ᎣᎦᎵᎪᏒ ᎪᎯᏅ ᏥᎦ ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎪᏭ ᏍᎪ ᏴᏩᎾᏗ
segments.transliteration: sge, dotsinogisgonv nole daninogisgo de dodvwideni usv ulitsvdvwadi yunaduli. nvgi uwanilv igohida dotsinogisgo yuwawedoli yuwogiyvtli. atsi idv doyu squisda dikanigisda dunvdv. dogate leyiga nigada heni ogaligosv gohinv tsiga aginulvhvsgowu sgo yvwanadi
segments.translation: And we would go and sing, or they would sing. Saturday night. All night. If they wanted—we would sing till four o’clock. When we would be goin’ and goin’ Arch really sang a lot. Or all of us knew them [songs] because we were together. Now’days I cannot even do that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Gah-lee.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏳᎵᎮᎵᏍᏕ ᎩᎶ ᏛᎬᏳᏂᏙᏗ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᎦᏓᏅᏖᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: yulihelisde gilo dvgvyunidodi yigehe nahiyu gelisgo gadanvtesgo
segments.translation: It would have been joyful—if someone could have recorded, back then. When I think about it.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: ᎾᏛ Ꮲ ᎠᏎ ᏱᎦᏰᎯ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎦ ᎠᏅ spavinaw ᎤᏃᎴ ᏭᎯᎸᏍᏛᏅ ᎤᎾ Ꮲ ᏥᎦᏁᎸ record ᏥᏂᏚᏩᏁᎸ ᏙᏥᏃᎩᏍᎬ tapes ᏃᎴ then Ꭵ plate Ꮫ ᏥᏚᏬᏢᏅ Ᏼ ᏗᏗᎩᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏅᎩ ᎢᏗᏍᏆ Ꮲ ᎨᎵ ᏥᏚᏬᏢᏅ ᎾᏅ Ꮲ carnival ᎠᏍᏆᎵᎲ ᏫᏚᏃᎩᏍᏕ ᎩᎶ ᎢᏯ ᏍᏈᏍᏛᏅ ᏴᏫ ᎠᏂᎷᎨ. ᏂᎦᏓ ᏚᏅᏕᏐᏁ ᎤᎾᎾ. ᏌᏭᏭ ᎢᎦ ᏍᏈᏍᏙᏒ ᎠᏕᎳ ᎠᎮ ᎤᏬᏢᏁ ᎾᎯᏳ. ᏓᏥᏱᏛᏛᏂ ᏳᎯ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏞᎠᎮ ᏍᎫ ᏱᏙᎬᎦᏛᏓᏍᏗ ᎠᏗᎲ ᎡᏙᏓ. ᎤᏓᏛᏛᏅ ᏌᏭ ᎠᎩ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ record ᏂᏙᏛᎬᏁᎵ ᎤᏛᏅ. ᎾᏅ ᎤᎯᏴ record ᏂᏚᏩᏁᎸ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏘ ᏂᏚᏩᏁᎸ. Ꮭ ᏯᎦᏛᏛᏁ ᎣᏂ ᏃᏭ films Ꭴ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏥᏅᏁᎸ Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏘ ᏄᏩᏛᏅ. ᎭᎫᏍᏗ ᏯᎦᏔᎮ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏍᎫ ᎠᏯ Ꮕ ᏍᎫ Ꮲ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏲᏥᎦᏔᎮ
segments.transliteration: nadv tlv ase yigayehi gohiyv tsiga anv spavinaw unole wuhilvsdvnv una tlv tsiganelv record tsiniduwanelv dotsinogisgv tapes nole then v plate dv tsiduwotlvnv yv didigida tsigehv nvgi idisqua tlv geli tsiduwotlvnv nanv tlv carnival asqualihv widunogisde gilo iya squisdvnv yvwi aniluge. nigada dunvdesone unana. sawuwu iga squisdosv adela ahe uwotlvne nahiyu. datsiyidvdvni yuhi sgi yusdi tleahe sgu yidogvgadvdasdi adihv edoda. udadvdvnv sawu agi sginana record nidodvgvneli udvnv. nanv uhiyv record niduwanelv tla yawati niduwanelv. tla yagadvdvne oni nowu films u yiga atsinvnelv tlv yawati nuwadvnv. hagusdi yagatahe edoda sgu aya nv sgu tlv gusdi yotsigatahe
segments.translation: That one—he probably would not be alive now. There at Spavinaw, where the tornado went through, he lived there, somewhere. He recorded us singing and made tapes and plates yea big [gestures]. I think he made about four-hundred. Somewhere at a carnival someone was playing them. Lots of people came and he sold all of them in one day. He must have made lots of money then. “I will ask him if he has one. But we probably would not listen to it,” my dad said. Dad asked. He said “I have one left and I am going to record.” The one he had left, he recorded. But I don’t know where he sent them. He [Dad] didn’t ask him. He just gave him a film. I don’t know where he sent it. I didn’t know anything, and we didn’t know anything.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎬᎵᎡᎵᎦ Ꮫ bud ᎡᎵᏭ ᎦᏨᏩᏛᎯᏓᏍᏗ ᏥᏂᎦᎵᏍᏛᏂᏓ ᏃᎴ ᏥᏍᎩᏃᏎᎸᏂᏛ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏗᏥᎶᏒ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏍᎫ ᏥᏃᎮᏢᎩ ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎦᏗᎭ ᎨᏐ ᎩᎶ ᏥᎦᏃᎮᏢᏍᎪ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏥᎦᏗᏍᎪ ᏙᎮᏂ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏱᎦᏬᏂ ᎩᎶ ᎧᏃᎮᏢᏍᎬ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏫᏓᏟᎶᏍᏙᏗ ᎨᏐ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎧᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎬᎵᎡᎵᎦ Ꮫ ᎡᎵᏭ ᎦᏨᎵᏃᎡᏙᏗ ᏥᏂᎦᎵᏍᏓᏂᏓ
segments.transliteration: gvlieliga dv bud eliwu gatsvwadvhidasdi tsinigalisdvnida nole tsisginoselvnidv nusdv ditsilosv nole sgu atsalagiha sgu tsinohetlvgi usquanigadiha geso gilo tsiganohetlvsgo atsalagiha tsigadisgo doheni atsalagiha yigawoni gilo kanohetlvsgv eliwu widatlilosdodi geso nusdv kanohesgv sgina yusdi gvlieliga dv eliwu gatsvlinoedodi tsinigalisdanida
segments.translation: I appreciate it, Bud. That you could come visit us, and all that you told us about what you have been through. And you talked about it in Cherokee. It is amazing that someone can talk about things in Cherokee. And uses it when someone is talking [also] in Cherokee. And talks about things. He paints a picture about what he is talking about. That is why I am thankful that I was able talk to you all.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎦ Ꮫ ᏙᎮᏂ ᎤᏚᏟᏙ Ꮩ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ Ꮩ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏢᏍᎪ ᏳᏓᎭ Ꮲ ᏱᏛᏝᏃᎮᏗ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎬᎵᎡᎵᎪ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏲᏙᎬᏢᏃᎮᏟ Ꮲ ᎠᏯ ᎨᏒ ᎣᏍᏕ ᎠᏩᏙ ᎠᏯ ᎨᏒ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎩᎶ ᎤᎵᏍᏕᏟᏙᏗ ᎤᎾ ᏳᏕᎳᏆ ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎦ ᎠᏯ ᎨᏒ
segments.transliteration: vv galieliga dv doheni udutlido do atsalagi advdasdodi do osda aninohetlvsgo yudaha tlv yidvtlanohedi sginana gvlieligo sgi yusdi yodogvtlvnohetli tlv aya gesv osde awado aya gesv aseno gilo ulisdetlidodi una yudelaqua galieliga aya gesv
segments.translation: OK, I am thankful. There really is a need to listen to Cherokee. If someone is talking and having a good conversation, somewhere, sometimes, they will talk to you. I appreciate that we talk like that, somewhere. As for me—I know it well. But if it is for someone else’s benefit and helping them with learning—I am thankful for that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎮᏂ ᏥᎾᏗᎲ ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎦᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎢᏗᏣᎳᎩ ᏗᎩᎶᏏ ᏕᎦᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᏃᎴ ᏧᏓᎴᏅᏗ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎩᏓ ᎢᎩᎪᎲᏂ
segments.transliteration: doheni tsinadihv usquanigadi heni iditsalagi digilosi degadvsidisv nole tsudalenvdi squu usquanigida igigohvni
segments.translation: Really. Like we said—it is amazing what us Cherokees have come through. Growing up and having seen different, amazing things. We see; we know where it begins—the amazing things we see.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎢᏗᎪᏩᏘᏍᎬ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎢᎦᏙ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᎤᎾ ᏕᏓᎴᏂᏍᎬ ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎦᏓ ᏥᏗᎪᏩᏗᏍᎪ ᏃᎴ ᏅᏍᏊ ᏗᎩᎶᏒ ᏍᎫ ᏕᎦᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᏍᎫ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᎢᎨᎾ ᏱᎨᏎ
segments.transliteration: idigowatisgv asena igado heni squu una dedalenisgv usquanigada tsidigowadisgo nole nvsquu digilosv sgu degadvsidisv sgu hesdi heni squu igena yigese
segments.translation: In our past, growing up, we did not have lots of things.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.translation: No, really we didn’t.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.text: ᏍᎫ ᏛᏅ ᏥᎬᏃᏎᎲ ᎠᏙᏩᏛ ᏬᏥᎶᏍᎬ ᏃᎴ ᎠᏎᏒᏱᎡᏗ ᎬᎾᏗᎩ ᎣᏥᏁᎲ ᏙᏍᏗᎴᏴᏍᏗᏍᎬ ᎡᏙᏗ ᏃᎴ ᏙᏍᏗᏍᏆᎸᏍᎬ ᏍᎫ Ꮫ ᏙᏍᏛᏟᎶᏍᎬ ᏃᎴᏅ ᎠᏥ ᎣᏂ ᏣᎢᏐ ᎦᏅᏩᎶᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᎪᏍᏓᏯ ᏌᏩᎦᏗ ᏃᎴᏅ ᏗᏓ Ꮩ ᏥᏓᏃᎮᎰ Ꮕ wedge ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏕᎦᎲᏛᏍᎪ ᏓᏍᎷᏍᎬ ᏂᏕᎦᎵᏍᏗᎰ ᎾᏅ ᏱᏚᏔᏠᏂ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎤᎾ Ꮓ Ꮎ ᎦᎷᏍᏗ ᎤᏔᏂ ᎠᏍᎫᏍᎪᏛ ᎠᏫᏛ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎰ ᏙᏳ ᎠᎯᏓ ᎾᏛᏁᎲ ᎠᏏᎾᏏ Ꮫ ᎨᎲ Ᏼ ᏂᎩᏗ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏓ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏬᏟᏂ ᏃᎴ Ꮠ Ꮠ ᏃᎴ ᏅᎩ ᎯᏍᎩ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎬ ᏦᏍᏗᏛ ᏧᏍᏗᎭ Ꮫ ᏫᏙᎦᏟᎰᏅ ᏃᎴ ᎤᏁᎳᎩ ᏂᎦᏓ Ꮲ ᏚᏪᏙ ᎩᎶᏫᏛ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ᎾᏅ ᎦᎷᏍᏗ ᏗᏲᏟᏙᏗ ᏗᏲᏟ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎰ ᏌᏩᎦᏗ ᎪᏍᏓᏯ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎬᏗᎰ Ꭿ ᏱᏂᎬᏁᎵ ᏃᎴ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏗᏝ ᎠᎬᏛᎭᏍᏗᎲ ᏃᎴ ᏏᏭ. Ꮓ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ ᎠᏔᏬᎢᏙᎲ ᎤᎾ ᎧᎶᏫ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᎠᏍᏆᏗᎰ ᏙᏳ ᎠᏏᎾᏏ Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏥ
segments.transliteration: sgu dvnv tsigvnosehv adowadv wotsilosgv nole asesvyiedi gvnadigi otsinehv dosdileyvsdisgv edodi nole dosdisqualvsgv sgu dv dosdvtlilosgv nolenv atsi oni tsaiso ganvwalosdi na gosdaya sawagadi nolenv dida do tsidanoheho nv wedge sginana degahvdvsgo daslusgv nidegalisdiho nanv yidutatloni yusdi una no na galusdi utani asgusgodv awidv nigalisdiho doyu ahida nadvnehv asinasi dv gehv yv nigidi yiga ada sawu yuwotlini nole so so nole nvgi hisgi leyiga degotlvsgv tsosdidv tsusdiha dv widogatlihonv nole unelagi nigada tlv duwedo gilowidv yigohida nanv galusdi diyotlidodi diyotli yusdi tsigeho sawagadi gosdaya sgina yusdi gvdiho hi yinigvneli nole ahani ditla agvdvhasdihv nole siwu. no sdigida atawoidohv una kalowi igohida asquadiho doyu asinasi dv tsigehv atsi
segments.translation: That I was telling [before]—we went to the woods, and back and forth. We would carry two, and cut them down, and chop them up. We measured, and Arch would be walking behind us—sharp hammer on one side. And, what do they call them, wedges? That he would stick in, to split [the wood]. And, when they would kind of open up, then he would use a big axe to split. It would do this. He did it easy. He was experienced. And if the wood was this big [gestures] he would make one, then another, then another. He would make four or five good ones, ‘same size. He would sharpen them. When he sharpened them he would stand them up real quick. And that broad axe, it was kind of small, one side was sharp—he used one like that. He would peel the bark of one side, then the other. Then he would turn it around and then comb it a little, there. He would finish real quick. Yeah, he was experienced—Arch.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Some were experienced to cut.

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.translation: Really, he was gifted good.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: well, ᎢᏨᎵᎡᎵᏥᏍᎢ Ꭰ bud ᎡᎵᏭ ᎦᏣᎵᏃᎮᏙᏗ ᏥᏂᎦᎵᏍᏓᏂᎦ...
segments.transliteration: well, itsvlielitsisi a bud eliwu gatsalinohedodi tsinigalisdaniga...
segments.translation: Well, we appreciated you Bud. That we were able to talk to you...

segments.speaker: bud-foreman
segments.translation: Yes

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: ...and also maybe later we can talk again.
